# Spinach

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="spinach-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="spinach-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="spinach-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Spinach accumulates more cadmium than most vegetables, with retail medians from about 20 to 200 µg/kg fresh weight and some lots above the EU limit of 0.20 mg/kg; lead and arsenic are usually low in retail spinach but rise sharply on wastewater-irrigated and industrial sites.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<ul>
<li>
<strong>Metals of concern:</strong>

Cadmium in ordinary spinach; lead and nickel where fields are polluted; aluminium is naturally high.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Soil cadmium and chloride, irrigation water and industrial sites; freezing, cooking and washing do not reliably lower cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for fresh-weight cadmium and lead results by lot with the growing site and irrigation source.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</li>
</ul>
</section>

## Spinach overview

<a id="which-evidence-gaps-most-limit-those-decisions"></a>

Cadmium is the metal that decides most spinach questions.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Spinach takes cadmium up from soil and moves it into the leaf, and the large monitoring datasets agree that ordinary retail spinach carries tens to a few hundred micrograms per kilogram on a fresh-weight basis: a median of 40 µg/kg across 2,077 randomly sampled European submissions to WHO GEMS/Food, 125 µg/kg in submissions from the Americas and 200 µg/kg in US Total Diet Study composites from 2018 to 2020.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug 2007 summarised by EFSA gave a median of 50 µg/kg and a mean of 61.5 µg/kg, against 23.1 µg/kg for other leafy vegetables.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" EU maximum of 0.20 mg/kg for spinach, 105 of 2,262 raw spinach results in GEMS/Food and 10 of 27 US market composites were above the limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a <div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-spinach" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-spinach-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one spinach form, subgroup and metal; a mean, median and range from the same samples are separate rows. Ratings place a reported mean, median or sample result against a pooled HMI reference for the same spinach form and basis (fresh or dry weight), built from retail, monitoring and ordinary farm samples. Results from wastewater-irrigated, industrial or polluted sites are positioned against that reference but never set it. Same-study comparisons set a site, irrigation source or fertiliser treatment against its own control or study total. Held rows failed a check against their own paper and are shown but not compared.</p>

Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations, fresh-weight and dry-weight results are never converted into each other, and results from wastewater-irrigated, industrial or polluted sites, fertiliser trials and manufacturer tests are compared against the reference but never set it.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1–Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>An evidence-library reference for one spinach form and basis, not a probability sample of any market. GEMS/Food regions are reporting regions, not growing origins. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA TDS FY2018–FY2020</a></li><li><a href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements" class="internal" data-slug="sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements" data-no-cite-meta>Martin-Leon et al. 2023</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Method: hmi-pooled-reference-v2.</p><p>hmi-pooled-reference-v2:spinach-u-spinach-fresh-weight:a1d1a1b9371c</p><p>The reference is computed by HMI from admitted evidence, not copied from a study baseline. It describes the evidence currently in this scope; it is not a worldwide or current-lot benchmark. Source, year and region filters do not change it. Different HMI scopes are not one common ranking.</p></details></div></details><div hidden data-form-reasons><p data-reason="no_numeric_value_or_bound" data-title="Spread or extreme value only">The source reports only a percentile, range or maximum for these samples, with no mean or median to place against the reference. Spinach takes cadmium up through its roots and moves it readily to the leaves, while lead binds strongly in soil and moves little into leaves, so leaf lead mostly reflects soil or dust on the surface.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Chloride in soil or irrigation water makes cadmium more mobile and available to the plant, and older leaves accumulate more cadmium than young leaves because uptake follows transpiration.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Fertiliser and manure choices change lead and arsenic more than cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer">compared to the chemical fertilizer. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No study in the library compares field-grown with greenhouse or hydroponic spinach for any metal, so no growing-system preference can be stated; organic spinach appears in only two GEMS/Food cadmium results, too few to compare.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-frozen-or-canned-spinach-lower-in-cadmium-than-fresh" data-anchor="is-frozen-or-canned-spinach-lower-in-cadmium-than-fresh" data-question="Is frozen or canned spinach lower in cadmium than fresh?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is frozen or canned spinach lower in cadmium than fresh?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not in the monitoring data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European frozen spinach had a higher cadmium median (71 µg/kg) than raw spinach (40 µg/kg), and the single canned European result was 130 µg/kg; these are different samples, so the comparison does not show what processing does to a given lot.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>


<a id="processing-effects"></a>
<a id="ingredient-derivative-risk"></a>
<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Freezing, cooking, washing and purée

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Freezing, cooking and canning did not lower cadmium in the monitoring data.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In randomly sampled European GEMS/Food submissions, frozen spinach had a cadmium median of 71 µg/kg and cooked spinach 66 µg/kg, against 40 µg/kg for raw; in the Americas cooked spinach (116 µg/kg) was close to raw (125 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> These are different samples, not paired before-and-after measurements, so the differences cannot be read as an effect of processing; cooking does drive off water, which concentrates cadmium per kilogram of cooked leaf.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Washing removes soil and dust but little of the cadmium inside the leaf.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The 2024 review estimates that leaf washing lowers spinach cadmium by only about 8–15%, compared with 20–80% for zinc amendment of soil.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Boiling in clean water removed 3–31% of the arsenic from greenhouse spinach, but boiling market spinach in water containing 1,000 µg/L arsenic raised it from 0.01 to 0.75 µg/g fresh mass, so the cooking water itself can add arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Spinach purée and canned spinach behave as concentrated or prepared forms.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Economic and Consumer Policy · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Baby Foods Are Tainted with Dangerous Levels of Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Staff Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cadmium in spinach purée tested by a US baby-food manufacturer before use (143 µg/kg) was in the same range as its fresh spinach lots (101–142 µg/kg), and canned spinach in the Americas had a lead median of 8.5 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Economic and Consumer Policy · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Baby Foods Are Tainted with Dangerous Levels of Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Staff Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The library holds no paired measurement of a spinach purée or canned product and the leaves that went into it.


<a id="additional-geographic-and-remediation-evidence"></a>
<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Controls for spinach

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Controls for spinach act mainly where it grows: choosing the field, the irrigation water and the soil inputs.<sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In pot trials, zinc added to cadmium-spiked soil at 300 mg/kg lowered spinach leaf cadmium from 3.29 to 1.96 mg/kg dry weight, while 30 mg/kg had no effect, and acidified biochar at 1.2% lowered shoot cadmium by 33–59%.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hussain2016-spinach-cadmium-zinc|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tajammal Hussain, Ghulam Murtaza, Abdul Ghafoor, Mumtaz Akhtar Cheema · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hussain2016-spinach-cadmium-zinc">The Cd:Zn ratio in a soil affects Cd toxicity in spinach (Spinacea oleracea L.)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pakistan Journal of Agricultural Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hussain2016-spinach-cadmium-zinc">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/sheikh2025-spinach-biochar-cadmium|29]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Laraib Sheikh, Nargis Naz, Sadaf Oranab, Uzma Younis, Abdullah A. Alarfaj, Sulaiman Ali Alharbi, Mohammad Javed Ansari · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/sheikh2025-spinach-biochar-cadmium">Minimization of cadmium toxicity and improvement in growth and biochemical attributes of spinach by using acidified biochar</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/sheikh2025-spinach-biochar-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The 2024 review rates lime with zinc and limiting chloride inputs as the most effective field measures, at about 60% and 40% cadmium reduction, and cultivar choice at 0–50%.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

For lead and arsenic the controls are site and water rather than amendments.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer">compared to the chemical fertilizer. <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-do-some-studies-report-extreme-values" data-anchor="why-do-some-studies-report-extreme-values" data-question="Why do some studies report extreme values?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why do some studies report extreme values?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Some extreme values do not survive a check against their own papers. In a Dhaka market study every detected lead value was below the method’s own detection limit, and in an Iranian field study the cadmium standard deviation was eleven times the mean.<sup Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" same leaves raw.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No source in the library measured metals in a finished spinach product together with the spinach that went into it, so finished-product concentrations cannot be inferred from the leaf values here.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Spinach FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-spinach" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-spinach" data-question="What heavy metals are found in spinach?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in spinach?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Cadmium is found in almost every spinach sample and is the one most often at levels that matter.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Lead, total and inorganic arsenic, mercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin and uranium have also been measured; in monitored retail spinach lead and arsenic are usually low and mercury mostly below detection.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-does-spinach-contain-cadmium" data-anchor="why-does-spinach-contain-cadmium" data-question="Why does spinach contain cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why does spinach contain cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Spinach roots take cadmium up from soil and the plant moves it into the leaves, more readily than lead; chloride in soil or water increases its uptake.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Spiking pot soil with 3 mg/kg cadmium raised leaf cadmium from 0.01 to 3.29 mg/kg dry weight.<sup class="cite">[[sources/hussain2016-spinach-cadmium-zinc|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Tajammal Hussain, Ghulam Murtaza, Abdul Ghafoor, Mumtaz Akhtar Cheema · 2016</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/hussain2016-spinach-cadmium-zinc">The Cd:Zn ratio in a soil affects Cd toxicity in spinach (Spinacea oleracea L.)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Pakistan Journal of Agricultural Sciences</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/hussain2016-spinach-cadmium-zinc">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-there-a-legal-limit-for-cadmium-in-spinach" data-anchor="is-there-a-legal-limit-for-cadmium-in-spinach" data-question="Is there a legal limit for cadmium in spinach?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is there a legal limit for cadmium in spinach?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in several markets.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/mfds2012-food-code-heavy-metals|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Korea Food and Drug Administration · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mfds2012-food-code-heavy-metals">Article 2. Common Standards and Specifications for General Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Korean Food Code</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mfds2012-food-code-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The EU maximum is 0.20 mg/kg wet weight for spinach and similar leaves, and Korea, China and Hong Kong set 0.2 mg/kg for spinach or leafy vegetables; lead limits are 0.3 mg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/mfds2012-food-code-heavy-metals|32]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Korea Food and Drug Administration · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mfds2012-food-code-heavy-metals">Article 2. Common Standards and Specifications for General Foods</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Korean Food Code</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mfds2012-food-code-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation|35]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, FAS China Staff (Beijing) · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation">China Releases the Standard for Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods (USDA FAS GAIN Report CH2023-0040, unofficial translation of GB 2762-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Global Agricultural Information Network (GAIN), Report Number CH2023-0040</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2019-hk-metallic-contamination-guidelines|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region · 2019</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2019-hk-metallic-contamination-guidelines">Guidelines on the Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) (Amendment) Regulation 2018</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service GAIN Report HK1922, relaying the Hong Kong Centre for Food Safety Guidelines for the Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) (Amendment) Regulation 2018 (Cap. 132V sub. leg.)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2019-hk-metallic-contamination-guidelines">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No US cadmium limit for spinach appears in the sources held; the 2024 US review evaluates US data against the EU value.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-often-does-spinach-exceed-the-cadmium-limit" data-anchor="how-often-does-spinach-exceed-the-cadmium-limit" data-question="How often does spinach exceed the cadmium limit?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How often does spinach exceed the cadmium limit?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In GEMS/Food, 105 of 2,262 raw spinach results (about 5%) were above 0.20 mg/kg, and EFSA counted 3.9% of EU samples above the limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> US market composites from 2018 to 2020 exceeded 0.20 mg/kg in 10 of 27 cases.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-growing-regions-produce-spinach-with-the-least-cadmium" data-anchor="which-growing-regions-produce-spinach-with-the-least-cadmium" data-question="Which growing regions produce spinach with the least cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which growing regions produce spinach with the least cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The supported answer is a site rather than a country: fields away from polluted irrigation water and industry.<sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/chemistry2022-bio-accumulation-of-heavy-metals-in-some-north|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">INDIAN LEAFY VEGETABLES AND QUANTIFICATION OF CONSUMER HEALTH RISK DUE TO THEIR DIETARY INTAKE SHAIL KULSHRESTHA Department of Chemistry, D. B. S. (P. G.) College, Dehradun, India ( · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/chemistry2022-bio-accumulation-of-heavy-metals-in-some-north">BIO-ACCUMULATION OF HEAVY METALS IN SOME NORTH</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/chemistry2022-bio-accumulation-of-heavy-metals-in-some-north">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Retail monitoring found lower medians in Europe (40 µg/kg) and Gran Canaria (21.5 µg/kg) than in the Americas (125 µg/kg) and US composites (200 µg/kg), but these record where spinach was bought, not where it grew.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A US review reports higher cadmium in recent California and Arizona spinach than in 1980s samples from lower-cadmium soils.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-baby-spinach-have-less-cadmium-than-mature-spinach" data-anchor="does-baby-spinach-have-less-cadmium-than-mature-spinach" data-question="Does baby spinach have less cadmium than mature spinach?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does baby spinach have less cadmium than mature spinach?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Probably, but the library holds only indirect evidence.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A 2024 review explains that older leaves accumulate more cadmium and cites a New Zealand field study in which baby spinach had lower cadmium than the later bunching crop; the only direct baby-spinach result in the library is one lead non-detect.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-organic-spinach-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-anchor="is-organic-spinach-lower-in-heavy-metals" data-question="Is organic spinach lower in heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is organic spinach lower in heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library cannot say.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Only two organic spinach cadmium results are in GEMS/Food, and the one fertiliser trial found that organic manures raised spinach lead four- to sevenfold while leaving cadmium almost unchanged.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer">compared to the chemical fertilizer. In organic fertilizer applications, heavy metal contents such as arsenic, chrome, cobalt, and nickel were found to</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-washing-spinach-remove-heavy-metals" data-anchor="does-washing-spinach-remove-heavy-metals" data-question="Does washing spinach remove heavy metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does washing spinach remove heavy metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only the part on the surface.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Washing removes soil and dust, which carry most surface lead, but the 2024 review estimates only an 8–15% cadmium reduction, because cadmium is inside the leaf.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-cooking-spinach-reduce-cadmium-or-arsenic" data-anchor="does-cooking-spinach-reduce-cadmium-or-arsenic" data-question="Does cooking spinach reduce cadmium or arsenic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does cooking spinach reduce cadmium or arsenic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Cooking does not destroy metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Boiling in clean water removed 3–31% of arsenic from spinach, but boiling in water with 1,000 µg/L arsenic raised spinach arsenic about 75-fold, and the water lost in cooking concentrates cadmium per gram.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|24]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Cooked spinach in monitoring data had cadmium medians similar to or above raw spinach.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-frozen-spinach-different-from-fresh" data-anchor="is-frozen-spinach-different-from-fresh" data-question="Is frozen spinach different from fresh?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is frozen spinach different from fresh?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not lower in cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> European frozen spinach had a cadmium median of 71 µg/kg against 40 µg/kg for raw, and a lead median below 20 µg/kg, similar to raw; these are different samples, not the same lots before and after freezing.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-do-some-studies-report-very-high-metal-levels-in-spinach" data-anchor="why-do-some-studies-report-very-high-metal-levels-in-spinach" data-question="Why do some studies report very high metal levels in spinach?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why do some studies report very high metal levels in spinach?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Most come from spinach grown on wastewater-irrigated or industrial sites, and many are on a dry-weight basis, about 14 times fresh-weight values.<sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-spinach-a-concern-for-babies-and-young-children" data-anchor="is-spinach-a-concern-for-babies-and-young-children" data-question="Is spinach a concern for babies and young children?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is spinach a concern for babies and young children?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Spinach is one of the cadmium sources identified for infant foods.<sup class="cite">[[sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Seyfferth AL, Limmer MA, Runkle BRK, Chaney RL · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Mitigating Toxic Metal Exposure Through Leafy Greens: A Comprehensive Review Contrasting Cadmium and Lead in Spinach</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GeoHealth</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/seyfferth2024-spinach-cd-pb-review">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Charles A. Barber, Marc Boyer, Jake A. Carter, Patrick J. Gray, Jennifer Fong Sam, Mesay M. Wolle · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us">Toxic elements in baby and young children&#39;s foods in the US and correlation to ingredients</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> An FDA survey found that 18 of 20 purées and mixtures with the highest cadmium listed tomato, spinach or carrot, and spinach and purée tested by a manufacturer before use carried 101–143 µg/kg cadmium.<sup class="cite">[[sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us|18]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Charles A. Barber, Marc Boyer, Jake A. Carter, Patrick J. Gray, Jennifer Fong Sam, Mesay M. Wolle · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us">Toxic elements in baby and young children&#39;s foods in the US and correlation to ingredients</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food Additives &amp; Contaminants: Part B</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/barber2025-baby-food-elements-us">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals|12]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Reform, Subcommittee on Economic and Consumer Policy · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Baby Foods Are Tainted with Dangerous Levels of Arsenic, Lead, Cadmium, and Mercury</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Staff Report</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/us-house-subcommittee2021-baby-foods-tainted-heavy-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> No authoritative serving guidance for spinach and metals is in the library.

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-aluminium-is-in-spinach" data-anchor="how-much-aluminium-is-in-spinach" data-question="How much aluminium is in spinach?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How much aluminium is in spinach?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

A lot compared with other leaves.<sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. <details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-the-arsenic-in-spinach-inorganic" data-anchor="is-the-arsenic-in-spinach-inorganic" data-question="Is the arsenic in spinach inorganic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is the arsenic in spinach inorganic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Mostly it is measured only as total arsenic, which was low in retail spinach (medians 5.9–8 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Where inorganic arsenic was measured directly it averaged 5 µg/kg in Hong Kong, and five of seven European submissions were below a 6 µg/kg reporting limit.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|27]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-should-a-buyer-ask-a-spinach-supplier-for" data-anchor="what-should-a-buyer-ask-a-spinach-supplier-for" data-question="What should a buyer ask a spinach supplier for?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What should a buyer ask a spinach supplier for?</summary>
